script: In 2014, a Lady Gaga video shoot ended up with an animal that never should have been on set. She was filming G.U.Y. at Hearst Castle when a trainer brought in a baby kangaroo, a goat, and a small, wide-eyed primate called a slow loris. The slow loris looks like a toy, but it's the only venomous primate alive - an elbow gland turns its bite into anaphylactic shock. During the shoot, the loris bit Gaga. She laughed it off, and every animal was cut from the final video. Wildlife groups were furious that nobody could explain how the trainer even had a slow loris - the species is protected everywhere and illegal to trade. They are targeted by the pet trade for looking cute on camera, and traffickers often clip their teeth out with pliers, no anaesthetic, so they cannot bite the humans handling them. A pop star got bitten by one of the most trafficked animals alive, on a set that should never have had it. Follow for stories nobody could invent.

metadata.title: Random But True: The Animal That Bit Lady Gaga
metadata.caption:
In 2014, Lady Gaga was filming her music video G.U.Y. at Hearst Castle when an animal trainer brought in a baby kangaroo, a goat, and a small, wide-eyed primate called a slow loris.

The slow loris looks like a stuffed toy, but it's the only venomous primate on Earth - a gland in its elbow can turn its bite into anaphylactic shock.

During the shoot, it bit Gaga. She laughed it off, and every animal was cut from the final video.

Wildlife groups were furious that nobody could explain how the trainer even had one in the first place - the species is protected everywhere and illegal to trade, and traffickers often clip their teeth out with pliers, no anaesthetic, just so the animal can't bite the humans handling it.
